title: Plural genitive of one-syllable long-vowel words
summary: Shorten the long vowel and use -iden or -itten: maa (“country”) → maiden.

objectives: Shorten the long vowel and use -iden or -itten: maa (“country”) → maiden.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A plural genitive refers to more than one person or thing. Its ending belongs to the plural modifier, not necessarily to the thing owned. Here the task is forming the word.
Shorten the long vowel and use -iden or -itten. Both endings are standard in the words taught here.
keyPoints: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.

steps: Shorten aa to a and add -iden or -itten: maiden or maitten.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Shorten ää to ä and add -iden or -itten: päiden or päitten.
